body:
`ForwardPerformanceVanillaEngine` scales missing vega, rho and
dividend rho without checking `Null<Real>()`. The resulting numbers
no longer match the sentinel, so the option accessors return them
instead of reporting "not provided".

Guard each result as `ForwardVanillaEngine` already does. Provided
Greeks retain their existing formulas; delta, gamma and theta are
unchanged.

A standalone implementation probe, not included in the test suite,
used spot 100, moneyness 1, r = 5%, q = 2%, volatility 20%,
Actual/365 (Fixed), reset after 90 days and expiry after 365 days:

| Wrapped engine | `84fbf0a0e` | With this change |
|---|---|---|
| `IntegralEngine` or `FdBlackScholesVanillaEngine` | All three Greeks ≈ 3.36112840081e36 | Each accessor reports "not provided" |
| `AnalyticEuropeanEngine` | Provides all three Greeks | Same values |

The large number is the default build's null sentinel multiplied by
`exp(-0.05*90/365)/100`: the factor includes division by spot.

`testPerformanceGreeksNotProvided` removes each Greek independently
from an analytic engine and also exercises `IntegralEngine`. It checks
missing-Greek messages, retained Greeks within 1e-12, and NPV within
1e-6.

Implementation validation on Linux used GCC 13.3.0, Boost 1.83.0,
Release and `QL_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR=ON`. The base header fails six
assertions in the new case. With the fix, all nine `ForwardOptionTests`
cases and `QuantoOptionTests` pass in C++17 and C++20. The quanto suite
does not cover composition with a partial-Greek performance engine.

AI disclosure: this was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5).

title: Keep missing Greeks unavailable in `ForwardPerformanceVanillaEngine`
